title: What are the other numbers in a 3 by 3 frame around p times q?
description: In a multiplication grid, every number is its row number times its column number. The row numbers and column numbers around the middle give all eight other numbers of the frame, and one corner is checked against the grid.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number in the grid is its row number times its column number, so moving up one row changes the row number, not the answer. Same method as the dot diagram and the expanded brackets before it.

source: Observe the multiplication grid. Each number inside the grid is formed by multiplying two numbers.
video_script.why: The child has seen a number grow by one and what it adds. Here the neighbours of a grid number are written as brackets.
video_script.substitution: Name the row number and the column number of the middle, step each one up and down by one, and multiply every pair.
video_script.anchor: the multiplication grid with a frame of three rows and three columns
video_script.payoff_line: Each number is its row number times its column number

final_answer.value: Top row (p − 1)(q − 1), (p − 1)q, (p − 1)(q + 1); middle row p(q − 1), pq, p(q + 1); bottom row (p + 1)(q − 1), (p + 1)q, (p + 1)(q + 1)
final_answer.spoken: the top row is p minus one times q minus one, p minus one times q, and p minus one times q plus one

never_show: the middle number minus one as the number above it
maths_rules: A number in the grid is its row number times its column number.
The middle is p × q, with row number p and column number q.
The row above has row number p − 1, and the row below has p + 1.
The column to the left has column number q − 1, and the column to the right has q + 1.
Check with p = 4, q = 6: (p − 1)(q + 1) = 3 × 7 = 21, which is in the grid.
video_script.design: One idea: neighbours in the grid change the row number or the column number, not the answer. Uses the method of the dot diagram video. The grid frame stays on the stage while the working builds up.

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step one, find the row numbers. The middle row has row number p.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The row above is one less, so its row number is p minus one.
<bookmark mark='down'/>The row below is one more, so its row number is p plus one.

marks.left: q − 1 is written for the column on the left
marks.right: q + 1 is written for the column on the right

narration: <bookmark mark='mid2'/>Step two, find the column numbers. The middle column has column number q.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The column on the left is one less, so its column number is q minus one.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The column on the right is one more, so its column number is q plus one.

<bookmark mark='cells'/>Multiply that by each column number in turn.
That gives three numbers, one in each column of the frame.

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Each number is its row number times its column number.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top row is p minus one times q minus one.

<bookmark mark='mid'/>The middle row is p times q minus one, p times q, and p times q plus one.
